notes: Modern Malvaceae placement is secure. Available floral descriptions separate yellow outer sterile structures from purple/red fertile stamens. This is an important false-positive risk because conspicuous stamen differentiation is not by itself the strict two-pollen-fate heteranthery state. The species is not promoted or asserted absent from Table S1.

Pre-2010 sources establish Bixaceae placement, pollen-only reward, poricidal anthers, buzz pollination, pollen removal/deposition and outcrossing. Morphological sources indicate unequal stamen positions/lengths, but a source-secure two-type feeding-versus-pollinating stamen function for this exact species has not been recovered.

Agalinis was historically treated near Scrophulariaceae and has dimorphic stamens, but modern placement is Orobanchaceae and a direct functional study reports no division of labour typical of heteranthery. It cannot resolve the APG-III Scrophulariaceae representative.

Pre-2010 literature documents specialized buzz-pollination mechanisms in Pedicularis under older Scrophulariaceae usage. APG III places Pedicularis in Orobanchaceae, so it cannot be used to fill the review's explicit Scrophulariaceae row without direct Table S1 evidence showing otherwise.

Torenia can show heteranthery-like functional differentiation, but the evidence recovered is post-2010 and APG III treats the lineage outside Scrophulariaceae. This is retained as a taxonomic false-positive guard, not a representative candidate.
